address_forms: `1000:xxxx` is a Ghidra label (Form A of `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md`) and, because the game's code segment is the load base, its OFF is also the image offset. `20ae:xxxx` is DGROUP. `0eed:` and `0f78:` are Form B runtime segments. `cs_offset` is the image offset of a Pascal shortstring's LENGTH byte -- the exact immediate of the `mov di,imm16` that pushes it -- and `file_offset` is that plus the 0x18d0-byte MZ header, which is what `data/strings.json` keys on.

bounded_on_the_right_by.note: `1000:defc` is the next verb's own buffer push and is also where both den exits land, so the range's right edge is an instruction boundary the handler itself jumps to, not a number picked to fit.

threshold_blocks_finding.claim: Blocks #1 and #2 are byte-identical; block #3 is a DIFFERENT predicate. Factoring all three into one helper would change behaviour.
threshold_blocks_finding.shared_prefix_note: The first 13 bytes -- both flag compares and the `jz +7` between them -- are identical in all three; only the fourth instruction's displacement (the `jnz` at `1000:d91b`/`1000:da7a`/`1000:dcc6`) differs, and blocks #1 and #2 agree even there.
threshold_blocks_finding.neither_implies_the_other: With k = level - (district-1)*10, block #1/#2 is `5k + cred >= 65` and block #3 is `2k + cred >= 40`. k=1, cred=38 satisfies #3 and not #1 (the `a` arm fires with no menu line); k=13, cred=0 satisfies #1 and not #3 (the menu offers `a` and the arm refuses silently).

fight_param_finding.claim: `FUN_1000_3d11` distinguishes exactly five values of its `param_1`: 0, 1, 3, 4 and 6. `param_1 == 5` -- what the `d` arm passes at `1000:ddf9` -- matches none of them and reaches the default arm `1000:3fa7`, the fight body, exactly as any other unlisted value would. `param_1 == 6` -- what the `hp` arm passes at `1000:dc58` -- shares the `1000:3d32` arm with 0 AND has an exclusive block of its own at `1000:57ce`. So the two den fights are NOT the same call as the wander's `param_1 == 0`.
fight_param_finding.method: TWO sweeps over one aligned decode from `FUN_1000_3d11`'s own entry `1000:3d11`, covering the 6971 bytes `data/functions.json` records for it (3043 instructions; the walk runs out of decodable bytes at image offset 0x584f, three bytes past the body's end at 0x584c). (1) every instruction whose ModRM addresses `[bp+0x4]` -- eight. (2) every `cmp al,imm8` (opcode 0x3c) -- five, and all five are the dispatch chain below. The SECOND sweep exists because the first is not enough on its own: `1000:3d24` copies the parameter into `al` and every later test is a REGISTER compare that no `[bp+0x4]` scan can see. A first draft of this record had only sweep (1) and asserted `param_1 == 5 has no compare of its own` from it, which is the inventory-that-stopped-searching defect `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md` names.

dispatch.note: `al` is not written anywhere between one link and the next: each miss either falls straight through to the next compare (`1000:3d29` -> `1000:3d2b`) or is one unconditional `jmp` sitting at the fall-through address (`1000:3d2f`) or the conditional branch's own target. That contiguity is what makes the register compares readable as parameter tests.

chain.miss_by: the `jmp` at 1000:3d2f, immediately at the fall-through
the branch's own target -- the DEFAULT arm

fight_param_finding.param_6: `1000:57ce cmp byte [bp+0x4],0x6` gives 6 alone `1000:57de add [0x38cb],ax` with `ax = district*20` (`1000:57d4`..`1000:57dc`) -- the errand's own понтовость reward, which lives inside the fight function and not in the den.
fight_param_finding.param_5: matches none of the five compares, so it reaches `1000:3fa7`. What that costs relative to `param_1 == 0`, which takes the `1000:3d32` arm instead, was NOT established here -- the arms themselves were not decoded.
fight_param_finding.consequence: `Game::run_combat` models no `param_1` at all (`grep -n 'fn run_combat' src/game.rs`), which `docs/re/gaps.md` already records as open. Task 28 cannot port either den fight without widening it.

port_reachability.claim: No arm of the den is unreachable in this port for want of a writer: every global any den gate reads is written somewhere in `src/`.
port_reachability.tier: flow for the original addresses; the port half cites the command that recomputes it, per `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md`
port_reachability.note: This is the answer to `unreachable in this port`: nothing here is dead for lack of a setter. What blocks the port is `fight_param_finding`, not reachability.

what_the_port_must_change.what: `Game::shop_turn` recognises exactly one den key, `a`. Six more exist and are established at compare addresses: `p` (`1000:db2c`), `r` (`1000:db81`), `hp` (`1000:dc04`), `s` (`1000:dc6d`), `d` (`1000:dd3c`), `w` (`1000:ded7`).

The whole one-shot menu `1000:d816`..`1000:dabb` is unported past `1000:d8b9`; `Game::print_den_intro`'s own doc already says so. Eleven more lines, four of them gated and two of them dimmed by a colour digit.

The three `[0x3695]`/`[0x369a]`/`cmp ax,0x28` blocks are NOT one helper. #1 (`1000:d90f`) and #2 (`1000:da6e`) are byte-identical and use `(level - (district-1)*10 - 5)*5 + cred >= 40`; #3 (`1000:dcba`, ported) uses `(level - (district-1)*10)*2 + cred >= 40`. Factoring all three together changes behaviour in both directions.
`p` and `r` are plain state edits and port directly.
`s` writes nothing at all and prints one or two lines; it ports directly.

`hp` and the `d` arm's cop branch both call `FUN_1000_3d11` with a `param_1` the port does not model (6 and 5). See `fight_param_finding`. The rest of `d` -- the two luck compares, the haul, the xp and `1000:2526` -- has no such obstacle.

The den's own `ReadLn` does not trim (`0eed:0216` only lowercases). `Game::shop_turn` trims; `docs/re/gaps.md`'s trimmed-prompt entry already owns that divergence and this map adds the den to its population, it does not open a new one.

An unrecognised key is SILENT and reprints only the prompt, never the menu (`1000:dede`). `Game::shop_turn` already behaves this way; recorded so the porting task does not add a `Непонятно` line that the original has no string for.

known_not_boundaries.note: Addresses this artifact NAMES but does not claim are instruction boundaries. `tools/test_den_arms.py` exempts exactly these from the boundary walk AND asserts that each really is not a boundary, so the exemption cannot be used to smuggle in a wrong address.

entries.why: `docs/re/save-format.md`'s xp row cites it for the level-up routine's first read of `20ae:38ce`. It is one byte into `1000:2535 mov ax,[0x38ce]` (`a1 ce 38`). Recorded as a finding against that document, not used as a citation here.

sweeps.note: The anchors `tools/test_den_arms.py` asserts SET EQUALITY against. Each is a count over the aligned decode of `1000:d802`..`1000:df06`; a wrong count reds the sweep, which is the point -- an inventory guarded by nothing is the defect `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md` names.
